summary: Match a value against object, array, literal, and wildcard patterns with optional guards, binding pattern names for the arm body and leaving an uncovered case to the compiler.

capabilities.requirement: Support pattern matching as an expression over discriminated unions.
Let a syntax class declare a field that only some of its rules bind.
Consume a pattern as token trees and recur into its nested patterns.
Emit the position and length of a captured repetition as numeric literals.
Claim an expression macro whose extent reaches past the expression, such as a trailing block.
Rename the subject temporary so it cannot capture a call-site binding.
Report an uncovered case where the match is written, rather than throwing when one arrives.

syntaxNotes: An arm is a pattern, an optional `if (...)` guard, `=>`, and an expression.
A lowercase identifier in a pattern binds; any other literal compares.
An object pattern may use shorthand `{ x }` to bind the property of that name.
`_` matches anything and binds nothing, and answers every remaining case.
Arms are tested in source order and the first match returns.
Without a wildcard the arms must answer the whole subject, which the compiler checks.
